ops.text: Indemnification. HDI shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless the Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (a) an allegation that the Site or any services or deliverables provided by HDI infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (b) HDI's breach of applicable law; (c) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data or Confidential Information caused by HDI; or (d) HDI's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The Company shall defend and indemnify HDI against third-party claims to the extent arising out of the Content provided by the Company or the Company's breach of applicable law. The indemnified Party shall give the indemnifying Party written notice of the claim, the indemnifying Party shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim, and the indemnified Party shall provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.

verification.notes: Fallback level is complete: the inserted Section 5.5 delivers all eight fallback elements in operative language — HDI's retention of generic tools and know-how, a perpetual/irrevocable/worldwide/royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense the Site and all other deliverables and work product for the Company's business, and a data-use limitation confined to processing solely to provide the services. Preferred level is not complete and the drafter should not claim it: there is no Company ownership statement, no assignment of deliverables from HDI, no express retention of HDI's pre-existing IP (only generic tools and know-how), no statement that the Company retains all rights in its data, and no no-joint-ownership sentence. The data-limitation sentence uses a category trigger ("belonging to, supplied by, or processed for the Company") rather than selected named data types, so it does not fail the Customer-Data scope test; it also imposes no standing HDI exploitation right. Minimality holds: the finding is a genuine gap (no IP/licence clause existed), the fix is a single concise inserted section, nothing outside the checklist was deleted or paraphrased, and no survival tail, expense allocation, indemnity or procedural extras were added. Reciting "the Site and any other deliverables and work product" is necessary because the Agreement defines no "Deliverables" term. Intent is preserved: Section 5.2 (artistic/editorial control, written acceptance, consent to publish), the General Manager provision and Section 8.1 confidentiality survive unchanged and do not contradict the new licence; no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created ("services" ties to the Services performed under the Agreement, and "Content" is used as elsewhere in the Agreement). Optional strengthening (rationale-level only, not a defect at the fallback): add "The Company retains all right, title and interest in its Content, user information and data" and "No intellectual property shall be jointly owned" if the counterparty will accept the preferred position.
